name: Split Squat
description: The split squat is a stationary lunge variation where the feet remain fixed in a staggered stance throughout the set. Unlike a walking or reverse lunge, there is no stepping involved — the lifter descends and ascends repeatedly from the same foot position. This makes it an excellent tool for single-leg strength development with greater stability than other lunge variations and a valuable precursor to the Bulgarian split squat.

execution.starting_position: Take a lunge stride and hold it — one foot forward, one foot back. The rear foot rests on its toes. The torso is upright.
execution.setup_instructions: Adjust stride length so the front shin is roughly vertical when the rear knee is near the floor. Hold dumbbells at the sides or use a barbell on the traps for load.
steps: Step 1: Position the feet in a staggered stance with enough stride length that the front shin stays close to vertical at the bottom.
Step 2: Brace the core. Lower the rear knee toward the floor by bending both the front and rear knee simultaneously.
Step 3: Descend until the rear knee is 1–2 cm above the floor.
Step 4: Drive through the front foot — heel and midfoot — to return to the starting position.
Step 5: Complete all reps on one leg before switching.
execution.breathing_instructions: Inhale as you lower. Exhale as you return to standing.
common_mistakes: Stride too short — front knee drifts far over the toe
Leaning forward excessively — keep the torso upright
Pushing off the rear toes instead of emphasizing the front leg
safety_considerations: If the front knee is painful, check foot position and reduce stride length
execution.range_of_motion_guidance: Rear knee to within 1–2 cm of floor. Full standing extension at the top.
coaching_cues: Drop the rear knee straight down
Front foot drives the work — not the rear
